title: Alex Hormozi on Jay Shetty: first dollar, core four, closer, and money models
summary: Hormozi explains how to go from zero to first income: work for free for qualified people, use the Core Four to promote, the CLOSER framework to sell, and volume (rule of 100) to improve. He also covers money models, mindset around fear, criticism and focus, and why active income beats speculation.

principles.text: Skip speculation; increase money per unit of time by building income-generating skills (promote, convert, deliver).
principles.quote: I think of just money per unit of time. And that kind of takes out this binary or what I would consider a false binary of active and passive

principles.text: Get first clients with a 10 by 10 free offer: ten people, ten hours, one-on-one, to learn, earn testimonials, and discover the offer.
principles.quote: Just 10 by 10. So give 10 people 10 hours. And so you can say, "Hey, I'm going to do 10 hours of work for free." That is a really compelling offer.

principles.text: Raise price 20% every five customers until people stop saying yes.
principles.quote: you just keep bumping the price by 20% every five people until eventually people start stop saying yes.

principles.text: Volatility comes from insufficient volume; do 100 reachouts, 100 minutes of content or $100 of ads daily, then double down on the top 10%.
principles.quote: volatility is a symptom of insufficient volume.

principles.text: Persuade by stating facts and telling the truth, including damaging admissions; it cuts imposter anxiety and builds trust.
principles.quote: you'll be significantly more persuasive and have less anxiety by just stating the facts and tell the truth.

principles.text: A money model collects enough cash from one customer in 30 days to acquire and serve two more; a superior one gives padding to be bad elsewhere.
principles.quote: you collect enough cash from one customer in the first 30 days to get and service two more customers.
